rules.rule: Answer the exact dimension of the question, especially when the professor asks about formation, not just content.
rules.reason: The professor repeatedly stopped students who described the idea itself instead of explaining how that idea was formed.

rules.rule: For essays, use personal examples and self-reflection instead of giving a clean textbook summary.
rules.reason: The professor explicitly said that generic, AI-like answers are weaker than answers built from one?s own case and insight.

rules.rule: When explaining a norm or effect, name the actor, the mechanism, and the pressure point.
rules.reason: The class was repeatedly pushed from abstract claims toward who influences whom and through what route.

rules.rule: Do not stop at reporting an interesting response; interpret what it reveals about variation, media influence, peer comparison, or cultural expectation.
rules.reason: The professor kept moving students from anecdote to interpretation, especially around age variation and social influence.

rules.rule: Treat age norms as including sequence as well as timing.
rules.reason: The lecture explicitly expanded age norms from "when things happen" to "in what order events are expected to happen."

rules.rule: Separate what society treats as the appropriate age from what the speaker personally wants.
rules.reason: The professor clearly distinguished social age norms from personal plans or preferences.

rules.rule: When discussing theory, prioritize the current major frameworks and explain why they became central.
rules.reason: The professor gave an explicit hierarchy: life-span development and life-course perspective are the main frameworks now.

rules.rule: Use English theory names when they clarify meaning, especially for older theories and paired concepts.
rules.reason: The professor repeatedly switched to English labels to make theoretical contrasts more precise.

rules.rule: For life-course answers, connect theory to historical context, turning points, linked lives, and human agency.
rules.reason: The professor treated these as the core analytic moves needed to understand aging beyond stage theory.

rules.rule: For interview-based work, choose a target who can give detailed narrative material and then analyze the interview with life-course concepts.
rules.reason: The assignment briefing stressed story density, informed target choice, ethical recording, and post-interview analysis using life-course concepts.
